macro.regime: Hawkish ISM/Fed-Hike Repricing Collides With Record AI-Credit Stress as the Hormuz War-Premium Unwinds
macro.narrative: Brent and WTI crashed 11.40%/7.55% Monday (to $104.23/$96.26) after Iran signaled a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks with Washington -- unwinding essentially all of October's war-risk premium even though the Doha round technically closed 'without a breakthrough' and the plan is contingent on US sanctions relief; OPEC+ held December quotas steady on Nov 1, ruling out a supply-side explanation. That relief was overwhelmed by a hawkish data surprise: October ISM Manufacturing beat at 55.5 (vs 54.5 consensus/previous), its 10th straight expansionary month, with Production at a five-year high even as Prices Paid stayed ~25pts above neutral -- a mix that has swung CME-implied Fed-funds pricing toward roughly a 75% probability of a December HIKE rather than the cut debate markets had been running. Credit stress deepened on top of that: CCC-rated high-yield spreads widened to ~12%, the highest since November 2022, and hyperscaler CDS hit outright records (Oracle's 5-year CDS above 220bp, topping its 2008 level; Meta's at a record 114.79bp) after Meta's first negative free cash flow since 2012. Gold/silver/GDX (+1.65%/+2.17%/+2.67%) and VIX (+8.91% to 21.15 despite the S&P's mild -0.51% decline) both jumped Monday on a mix of US midterm-election hedging (elections today) and the credit-stress/safe-haven bid, a divergence consistent with markets pricing event risk -- today's RBA decision (31-of-32 economists expect a hike to 4.85%), the China rare-earth truce deadline, and the midterms -- rather than holding a resolved directional view. The rare-earth truce remains a live binary: Washington and Beijing have both verbally confirmed an extension to Jan 10, 2027, but China's governing Announcement No. 70 still legally expires Nov 10, 2026 with no superseding text published, keeping MP/Lynas/UUUU/USAR volatile into the deadline.

drivers.factor: Iran/Hormuz de-escalation signal collapses the oil risk premium

Doha talks technically ended 'without a breakthrough,' so this is a de-escalation signal, not yet a signed deal, leaving room for reversal.

drivers.factor: ISM Manufacturing beats hot, flipping Fed-funds pricing toward a hike
drivers.read: October ISM printed 55.5% (vs 54.5 consensus/previous), a 10th straight expansionary month, with Production at 59.0 (best since Nov 2021) and Prices Paid still 75.2 even as Employment slipped to 52.4 -- a 'manufacturing stagflation' mix that has swung CME-implied Fed-funds pricing toward roughly a 75% probability of a 25bp hike at the Dec 9 FOMC.

drivers.factor: Hyperscaler/AI-capex credit stress hits fresh records
drivers.read: CCC-rated spreads widened to ~12%, the highest since Nov 2022; Oracle's 5-year CDS topped 220bp (above its 2008 level) and Meta's hit a record 114.79bp after Meta's first negative FCF since 2012 -- an acceleration, not a stabilization, of the credit-stress theme.

drivers.factor: VIX decouples from equities on event-risk hedging
drivers.read: VIX jumped 8.91% to 21.15 even as the S&P fell only 0.51% to 7541.40 -- consistent with hedging into today's US midterm elections and RBA decision rather than a directional equity call; Dow actually rose 0.41% on lower energy input costs even as Nasdaq fell 1.07% on AI-capex/credit concerns.

RBA is priced for a near-certain (31/32 economists) hike to 4.85% today, AUD already softening pre-decision toward US$0.70; BOE is expected to hike to 4.00% Nov 5 (7-0-2 vote forecast); combined with the Fed's own hawkish repricing, this is a broad-based headwind for duration.

drivers.factor: China rare-earth truce legal-text gap persists
drivers.read: Washington and Beijing have verbally confirmed extending the truce to Jan 10 2027, but China's governing Announcement No. 70 still legally expires Nov 10 2026 with no superseding notice published, and the separate April-2025 heavy-rare-earth (Dy/Tb) licensing regime was never part of the pause -- the deadline risk for MP/Lynas/UUUU/USAR stays fully live for another week.
